title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། དབུ་མ། ཟ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 101)
shelf_note: Madhyamaka (dbu ma) volume of the Derge Tengyur; all four pages are prose commentary (refutation of Sāṃkhya, causality, Buddha-qualities, Madhyamaka critique of pramāṇa). Belongs on a Tengyur prose shelf.
structure_note: 681 records, 680 with OCR and 680 translated (one page without text, likely the cover or title leaf). Scan numbers in the left margin run one ahead of page_number (image 143 for page 142, 671 for 670): a constant offset, not a defect. No printed_backsteps or repeats. The book is visible:false.
reader_summary: A Madhyamaka commentary volume of the Derge Tengyur. The Tibetan is the Esukhia etext and matches the leaf line for line on all four pages checked, so the transcription is of the right text. The English follows the argument closely; on the denser logic pages it garbles some syllogistic steps and mistranslates a few analogies, so a specialist should check it against the Tibetan before quoting it.

tr_errors.english: To refute the invalidity of their system
tr_errors.problem: awkward: means 'to refute their system as untenable'

tr_errors.english: two contradictory actions—producing light and clearing darkness
tr_errors.problem: the source pairs light and darkness as the contradictory actions; 'producing light and clearing darkness' are not contradictory, so the analogy no longer works

tr_errors.english: afflictions, purification, and stability
tr_errors.problem: ལྡང་བ is 'emergence' (from absorption), not 'stability'

tr_errors.english: numbered 1–18 with 'regarding the present' left unnumbered
tr_errors.problem: translator-added numbering does not fit the source list (19 items as written)

other.note: summary adds 'within the Madhyamika framework of conventional truth', which the page does not say

ocr_errors.problem: the etext's variant-reading braces appear in the transcription

tr_errors.english: This is because even when such a statement is made the subject of a thesis, it is shown to be invalid, just as something invalidated by later reasoning is invalid, precisely because it possesses the nature of having parts.
tr_errors.problem: the source gives a counter-syllogism (thesis: such a statement is not a proof; reason: it has complete members; example: one invalidated by later reasoning). The English blurs it, so the structure of the argument is lost

tr_errors.english: this internal position of the opponents
tr_errors.problem: means 'anticipated objection' (pūrvapakṣa)

tr_errors.english: specific instances of refutation and the reality of the thing itself
tr_errors.problem: དེ་ཁོ་ན here is the genuine refutation (as opposed to pseudo-refutation), not 'the reality of the thing itself'

book_verdict: The Tibetan is right on every page. The English is good on expository pages and weaker on dense pramāṇa argument, with no serious errors in the four pages.

title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། ཤེར་ཕྱིན། ག (Derge Tengyur, vol. 82)
shelf_note: Prajñāpāramitā (sher phyin) volume of the Tengyur. All four pages are long verbatim runs of Perfection of Wisdom sutra text (Śāriputra–Subhūti dialogue, Ānanda and the smile) as quoted within a commentary. This is expected for this section.
structure_note: 629 records, 628 with OCR and 628 translated (one leaf without text). Margin leaf numbers run one ahead of page_number, a constant offset. Nothing else stands out. The book is visible:false.
reader_summary: A Prajñāpāramitā volume of the Tengyur, mostly sutra text quoted at length. The Tibetan matches the leaf on all four pages but carries stray '#' etext markers. The English is faithful and plain. One page adds invented markdown headings ('# Continuing from the previous section'), and some technical terms are rendered loosely.

ocr_errors.image: no such marks on the leaf

tr_errors.english: exhaustion
tr_errors.problem: upāyāsa is 'distress/despair'

other.note: invented markdown headings '# Continuing from the previous section' and '# On the nature of striving'. The first is also wrong: the passage is an abbreviation ('…up to…'), not a continuation from a previous page

tr_errors.english: the Buddhas and the Bhagavans
tr_errors.problem: one group (the Buddha-Bhagavans), split into two

tr_errors.english: not included within any category
tr_errors.problem: means 'not included (in the three realms)', aparyāpanna; 'any category' is a guess

tr_errors.english: is it that form is without attachment because there is no form?
tr_errors.problem: the source asks whether form is unattached to the absence of form, not whether this is because form is absent; the series is recast as causal

tr_errors.english: Suchness, unerring Suchness, unaltered Suchness; it is the non-erroneous reality just as it is. It would have to be an entity characterized as permanent…
tr_errors.problem: the page opens mid-conditional ('if mental contact were suchness…'). The English drops the 'if' for the opening clauses, so they read as an assertion

book_verdict: The Tibetan is right on every page (with '#' etext noise) and the English is faithful. The invented headings on page 106 are the visible blemish.

title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། རྒྱུད་འགྲེལ། དི (Derge Tengyur, vol. 42)
shelf_note: Tantra commentary (rgyud 'grel) volume. Pages 203, 260 and 436 are prose commentary. Page 57 is a verse sādhana (refuge, bodhicitta, maṇḍala visualisation), so the volume is not prose throughout. It is still on the right Tengyur shelf.
structure_note: 461 records, 460 with OCR and 460 translated (one leaf without text). The margin numbers run one ahead of page_number, a constant offset. Nothing else stands out. The book is visible:false.
reader_summary: A volume of tantric commentaries and sādhanas from the Tengyur. The Tibetan transcription matches the leaf on all four pages. The English is readable and mostly faithful. It misattributes a few points in technical passages (what is the 'seed', what abides 'within beings') and adds Sanskrit back-reconstructions labelled 'original:', which the Tibetan does not give.

tr_errors.english: Is the One Who Manifests Vairocana together with his awareness-consort, / Arising from the wheel of the syllable Bhrum and its components.
tr_errors.problem: the second line says it arises from Vairocana's limbs; the English makes Vairocana the subject and 'components' the wheel's. The grammar is loose but the sense is close

tr_errors.english: Fully liberated from every remnant of existence
tr_errors.problem: 'of existence' supplied; the line is the tail of a verse begun on the previous page

tr_errors.english: Although this state exists within all sentient beings in an infallible manner
tr_errors.problem: the source says Vajradhara abides in a way that does not deceive all beings; 'exists within all sentient beings' adds a buddha-nature claim

other.note: notes labelled 'original: "tattva"', 'original: "vidya-abhisheka"', 'original: "mahatman"' present Sanskrit back-reconstructions as the original wording of a Tibetan text

tr_errors.english: Furthermore, Vajradhara … is the seed that causes the realization of the nature of all Buddhas
tr_errors.problem: HŪṂ is the seed that accomplishes Vajradhara, the nature of all buddhas. The English makes Vajradhara the seed

other.note: the 'original: "dbyings"', 'original: "phung po"' notes repeat Tibetan words as glosses; harmless but cluttered

tr_errors.english: the Explanatory Tantra of the Glorious Chakrasamvara
tr_errors.problem: རྒྱུད་ཕྱི་མ is the Later (Uttara) Tantra, a different text-type from an explanatory tantra (bshad rgyud)

book_verdict: The Tibetan is right on every page and the English is usable. Several moderate misattributions in technical tantric passages mean a specialist should check it before citing.

title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། རྒྱུད་འགྲེལ། ཇི (Derge Tengyur, vol. 38)
shelf_note: Tantra-commentary volume containing Guhyasamāja commentaries (page 451 has the colophon of a root-tantra commentary and the opening of the Uttaratantra commentary). Prose throughout on these pages.
structure_note: 487 records, 486 with OCR but only 483 translated: three pages with text lack a translation. The margin numbers run one ahead of page_number, a constant offset. Nothing else stands out. The book is visible:false.
reader_summary: Guhyasamāja commentaries from the Derge Tengyur. The Tibetan matches the leaf on all four pages. The English tracks the commentary well, including the colophon and the chapter transition. It misreads some technical terms ('seeker' for the melted form, 'nine bodies'), and on one page it may reverse a reply in an argument. One page puts a translated sentence inside a <meta> wrapper.

ocr_errors.problem: the etext's variant-reading braces appear in the transcription

tr_errors.english: the women are emanated from the nine bodies
tr_errors.problem: nine women are emitted from the body; 'nine bodies' misparses the number

tr_errors.english: clearly appear in a formless manner
tr_errors.problem: 'signless', not 'formless'

other.note: the first translated sentence ('It is explained as "transcending the Vajra-holder."') sits inside a <meta> wrapper and will be lost or shown as meta
'->…<-' centring markers around the verse lines

tr_errors.english: so it does not obscure or eliminate the others
tr_errors.problem: the source has no negation ('…the others are obscured and become absent'). The English inserts 'does not', which may reverse the reply. Low confidence on the intended sense

tr_errors.english: applied only to the <note>original: "Supreme King of Mandalas"</note>
tr_errors.problem: the term itself is moved into a note, so the sentence reads 'only to the [note]'

tr_errors.english: transformed into the form of a seeker
tr_errors.problem: ཞུ་བ here is 'melted' (the melted form), not 'seeker'

tr_errors.english: Uttaratantra (gloss: Explanatory Tantra)
tr_errors.problem: Uttaratantra is the 'Later Tantra'; the gloss conflates it with an explanatory tantra

book_verdict: The Tibetan is right on every page and the English is mostly sound. A handful of moderate term misreads and a possibly reversed reply on page 263 mean it should be checked before quoting.
